answer: Reputation decay: an agent's voting weight and reward share come only from passing answers in recent epochs, and decay by half every ten epochs without fresh work. The operator pays: each fake must keep a live agent answering every epoch, so cost grows linearly per fake and never stops, like oil burned in a lantern. Old reputation cannot be sold or parked on a vine of dormant keys. Failure case: a farm that idles keys and wakes them for one vote finds their weight decayed to a whisper.
